name: SOL aligned-flow reversal
description: SOL: right after a 15-minute window opens, if the previous window moved more than 1.25 sigma and Binance taker flow in that window was one-sided in the direction of the move (net buy-sell share >= 0.25), buy the reversal side. One-sided aggressive flow behind a big move is forced/impatient flow that overshoots; two-sided or passive moves persist.
hypothesis: Dev screen (research dataset, SOL, top-decile |strike move| in rv units, mid 30-70c, next real fill after fee): reversal edge by tercile of the prior window's signed Binance taker imbalance aligned with the move: Jan-Apr +0.4/+3.8/+11.0c, May-Aug +2.2/-2.9/+5.7c; threshold curve >0.05 +3.8c, >0.2 +5.8c, >0.3 +7.1c (n=231), late-era (May-Aug) >0.3 +6.0c (n=123); top tercile positive in 6/7 months. Mechanism: one-sided aggressor flow = forced liquidations / momentum chasers who overpay, the opening quote ignores it. Losers: opening takers. Caveats: threshold 0.25 picked after seeing the dose curve (post hoc), flow-who (ETH/BTC/SOL, |z|>1.5, 30 s shocks) found one-sidedness uninformative, same family as sol-volrev (counts as one piece of evidence), paper/live need a live Binance flow stream. Wrong if: full CI<=0, <60% months positive, 2x latency loses, last 3 months flat, or lockbox loses.
